entities.name: the 汴河, middle reach (u 23300-26000)
entities.what: The river as plain silk with fine ink ripple motifs, filling the silk from the boats along the north bank (their hulls lie against the shore at v ~500-650) down to the silk's bottom edge; no south bank is painted in this reach. Three big boats fill its northern half: 逆水行舟 under tow, the high-sided cargo boat beside it and the boat moored before the halls; south of v ~1230 the water is open and empty to the silk's edge.
entities.vis: part: the north shore is hidden behind the moored boats all along the reach; the south runs off the silk
entities.note: shore_n is hidden everywhere (est, reading error about +-25 px): 23300-23700 behind 豪华客船 (river_w2) and the terrace stilts, whose feet reach the shore at v ~485-495 (t4); 23700-25150 behind the north side of the high-sided cargo boat (its bow deck at v ~575 and its deckhouse roof at v ~496-530 lie against the bank; the bank's dark wash runs v ~470-530 at 23600-24300 and v ~510-600 at 24700-25150); 25150-26000 below the bank's wash (v ~560-640) and the narrow bank strip in front of the halls (v ~555-640, t7), behind the moored boat's bow bitts, mat canopy and cabin roof (v ~600-680). No shore_s: east of u 22300 nothing is painted south of the water; the silk's bottom edge cuts it at v ~1776 all along 23300-26000. Ripple motifs (short paired curls) are drawn all over the open water, densest at v 1250-1650; nothing in this reach is drawn as a strong current (汴水悍激, pin 7, is further east, river_e). The restyle's east half paints u ~25500-26400, v 1000-1790 as dry grassy ground: it is water (the scan has the ripple lines). End points for the merge: west (23300, 492) joins river_w2, east (26000, 650) joins river_e. Merge: seam points set so the reaches join: west (23300, 496) est (the mean of river_w2's 500 and this unit's 492); east (26000, 665) est, river_e's (this unit had 650).

Merge: seam points set: west bank_top (23300, 452) est and shore (23300, 496) est (the means with river_w2); east bank_top (26000, 632) and shore (26000, 665) est, river_e's (the warehouse plinth's foot; this unit had 615 and 650). entities.name: 逆水行舟: the big passenger-cargo boat with a mast, towed upstream
entities.what: A long, deep river boat lying in mid-river south of the cargo boat, bow west, being towed upstream: a single mast stepped amidships in a braced tabernacle on the cabin roof at u ~24190, its top at (24183, 302), with a fan of about fifteen stays and lines to both ends of the deck; the tow rope is made fast to the mast at (24188, 375) and runs about 2350 px west over the cargo boat's bow, the bank and the water to the five trackers (t2: S2.grp.boat_towed_mast_23632; the rope's far end is in the lead tracker S2.fig.tracker_lead_21867's hands at (21832, 197)); a short bar is lashed across the rope at (23945, 435-472). A long plank-walled cabin with lattice windows and a door runs the whole length under a low mat roof (cabin walls v ~1030-1140); the bow at the west end has a dark arched mat hood over a low foredeck, a carved stem post and two boat-hooks lying crossed over the stem; the stern at the east end rises over a big rudder whose blade trails at the waterline (24965-25185, v 1160-1220), under a mat awning with a big coil of bamboo rope (24900-25000, v 840-930) and two light boards standing under it, a tall one at u 24732-24789 (v 869-979) and a shorter one just west of the coil at u 24866-24902 (v 920-975); a long dark mat-hatched blade projects east from the stern at deck level to (25285, 1010) (a sweep 橹 shipped aft, or the stern awning's eave). Coiled ropes and bundles on the roof. Crew: a bowman under the hood, a man fending off 豪华客船's stern with a pole, a robed man on the foredeck, three or four men on the roof (one kneeling and hauling a line at the mast), a passenger at a window (perhaps two) and a man at the stern cabin's door. Not moored: it passes the moored cargo boat on its south side, close alongside.
entities.vis: part: its north side is hidden behind its own roof; the bow waterline behind the crossed boat-hooks
entities.note: WHICH HULL CARRIES THE MAST: this (southern) one. The mast is drawn in front of the cargo boat's planking all the way down from v ~460 to its tabernacle on this boat's roof (posts at u ~24185 and ~24222, braces u 24180-24260, v 893-965); a mast stepped in the cargo boat would stop behind that boat's side. The tow rope ends at this mast. BOW: west (the end without the rudder; the lead's rule): the rudder and the projecting blade are at the east end, the hooded foredeck with the bowman at the west, and the trackers haul west. TOW ROPE (custom point rope, a polyline from the mast to the far end, scan px): mast (24188, 375) -> (24100, 400) -> (24016, 430) knot -> (23945, 450) the lashed bar -> (23700, 499) -> its lowest sag v ~518-521 at u 23250-23500 -> (22900, 491) (my reading, matching t3's) -> t3's and t2's readings to the lead tracker's hands at (21832, 197); it runs on through all five trackers' grips (t2). Length along u ~2356 px. FAR END: S2.fig.tracker_lead_21867 (t2), the whole file S2.grp.boat_towed_mast_23632 (t2). WATERLINE: beam_s = the hull's lowest near-side line, v 1200-1215 at u 24300-24900; the bow's waterline est where the stem's lower line meets the hull bottom (23632, ~1100); the stern's est under the sternpost behind the rudder (25050, ~1205); beam_n est (hidden), from the roof's depth (the roof spans v ~820-1000). SCALE CUE: hull 23632-25050 = about 1420 px at the waterline; mast 663 px from its foot to its top; hull side (gunwale wale v ~1140-1150 to bottom v ~1210) about 65 px; cabin wall about 110 px (v 1030-1140); window opening about 95 px tall; the crew on the foredeck about 125-133 px tall at foot v 950-1070. Freeboard for the frame: gunwale (24400, 1145) over waterline (24400, 1212), 67 px; the roof's front edge at v ~1000-1030 over the gunwale; the bow deck (23640, 1068) over its waterline (23640, 1100). Restyle: it adds a second man at the bow (u 23600-23640) where the scan has the carved stem post, and shows the blade at the stern as a blue fish-shaped object. "Rowed by eight men" (sections.md): no oar or sweep is in the water on the scan; the fan of long lines from the mast are stays, and only one man on the roof works a line. Second pass: the light shape under the stern awning at u 24866-24902, v 920-975 is a second, shorter board (retired man_stern_awning_24870 (retired at the second pass)), drawn like the tall one at 24732-24789; a possible second, smaller passenger at the cabin window (S2.fig.second_passenger_window_24050, low); the 'second figure beside the poler' (retired crewman_beside_poler_23748 (retired at the second pass)) is a fender hung from the cargo boat or a bitt post on this foredeck (both readings in the cargo boat's note). Crew 11 -> 10 or 11 with the new low passenger.

entities.name: high-sided cargo boat with a hooded bow, moored along the north bank
entities.what: A very long, high-sided boat lying along the north bank, bow west, close beside 逆水行舟 to its south and end to end with 豪华客船 to its west: at the bow (u 23700-23900) a curved arched beam over a dark mat hood, a deck post and a spoked windlass; on deck a flat board platform on legs and big round coils of rope or baskets (23940-24090, v 635-725) and a short ladder leaning from the deck up to the bank (top at (24045, 505)); amidships a flat mat-roofed deckhouse open at the sides (roof u 24275-24583, v 496-530) with a second arched beam and a dark mat hood at its east end (24425-24600, v 586-730); east of it a spoked wheel or windlass on a post (24640-24740, v 523-590); aft a huge rounded mat cover over the cargo, topped with a woven round basket (24775-25137, v 542-667); a high curved stern with a carved post and the rudder stock at u ~25100-25130. A coil or round fender hangs on its south side at (24380, 840), and at the bow a long rope-wrapped fender (or bundle) hangs on a line over its south side, between it and 逆水行舟's foredeck (u 23735-23768, v 745-872). No mast. Its many strakes with rivet rows show it riding high (unladen). Crew: a man at the bow (the spoked windlass beside him is unmanned), one or two men at the aft windlass, two crouching on deck, two in the deckhouse and a man poling at the gunwale.
entities.vis: part: its waterline and lower hull are hidden behind 逆水行舟 all along; its north side behind its own deck
entities.note: ONE HULL OR TWO: one. The rivet rows of its strakes run unbroken from the bow (u ~23710) to the stern (u ~25165) at v ~690-860 (checked at zoom 3 at u 24540-24820, where a second boat's bow would be). THE BRIEF'S "SMALL CANOPIED BOAT" (24250-24500, v 500-600) is read as this boat's midship deckhouse: its two seated men sit at v ~600, on this boat's deck level, and no separate hull, stem or waterline shows under it. Other reading (conf low): a small canopied boat lying in the gap between this boat and the bank, its own hull hidden; it would then need its own entity with the two men as its crew. BOW: west (the rudder stock and the high stern at the east end). WATERLINE: hidden; front and rear est at the feet of the stem and the sternpost where they disappear behind 逆水行舟 (v ~870-880); beam_s est; beam_n est at the deck's north edge (hidden). MOORED: it lies against the bank with its ladder up to it; no mooring rope to a post is visible in u 23700-25150. SCALE CUE: hull about 1430 px (23715-25145); the deck's south gunwale at v ~690-700 and the visible side down to v ~860-880 (about 180 px, much higher than 逆水行舟's 65 px side: riding high, or a higher-sided boat); its crew about 62-67 px tall at foot v ~575-600. Freeboard for the frame: gunwale (24400, 695) over the hidden waterline (24400, ~885 est). The restyle paints knots of 4-5 people at the bow windlass (23750-23980) and at the aft windlass (24600-24740): the scan has 3 and 2-3. Second pass: (1) the 'second figure beside the poler' (retired crewman_beside_poler_23748 (retired at the second pass)) is a long rope-wrapped fender or bundle hung on a line over this boat's south side at the bow: line from a small bar on the planking at (23742-23752, 744-749) down to a scroll-tied top (23731-23766, v 777-797), wrapped body to its tapered foot (23744, 872, est, behind 逆水行舟's bow hood); other reading: a bitt post with scroll ends on 逆水行舟's foredeck. (2) The bow windlass is unmanned on the scan (windlass_man_w_23888 (retired at the second pass) and windlass_man_e_23952 (retired at the second pass) retired as its disc, crank and spoke ends): the crew is 9, not 11. (3) A thin upright stick stands at the deckhouse roof's east end at (24537, 482-500) (t6 left it to river_m): a pole stood upright on the deck, or a stake on the bank behind the roof.
